description: Update WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md with final 10-model Bedrock scores from metacog_final_scores.csv
steps: Step 1: Read repo/results/metacog_final_scores.csv and extract per-benchmark mean, std, range across all 10 models
Step 2: Read current repo/WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md and identify the Results section

Step 3: Replace any placeholder or outdated score tables with the final 10-model data including three-tier pattern (external monitoring ~0.83, self-monitoring ~0.68, prospective ~0.29) and calibration floor finding (6/10 models BSS=0.000)
Step 4: Add key discriminatory insights: canary is best discriminator (std=0.305), calibration second (std=0.347), scale amplifies Tier 1 not Tier 3
Step 5: Ensure word count stays at or below 1500 words using wc -w
Step 6: Verify all 7 required template sections are present and populated

description: Harden metacog_fok benchmark to improve discrimination (current std=0.083, target >=0.10)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_fok.py and identify scoring logic (composite: 0.40*gamma + 0.30*BSS + 0.30*AUC)
Step 2: Analyze repo/results/metacog_final_scores.csv fok column — identify which models cluster and where spread is needed

Step 3: Add harder FOK items that frontier models should get right but weaker models cannot — e.g., multi-step reasoning FOK where the model must judge its ability to derive an answer through chained inference
Step 4: Add easier items that even weak models answer correctly to establish a floor — e.g., simple factual recall FOK items
Step 5: Run quick 3-model smoke test (Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B) using repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py on the updated benchmark
Step 6: Verify std >= 0.10 across the 3 test models; if not, adjust item difficulty distribution

description: Harden metacog_jol benchmark to improve discrimination (current std=0.091, target >=0.10)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_jol.py and the data module to understand current item set and scoring
Step 2: Analyze jol scores across 10 models from metacog_final_scores.csv — models cluster 0.30-0.50 with insufficient spread
Step 3: Add difficulty-stratified pseudoword items: 10 very easy (short, phonotactically regular) and 10 very hard (long, irregular, cross-language interference) to widen the JOL prediction gap
Step 4: Verify the gamma correlation computation has the division-by-zero guard (known bug from KNOWLEDGE)
Step 5: Run 3-model smoke test (Claude Opus 4.6, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B)
Step 6: Verify std >= 0.10; iterate on item difficulty if needed

description: Harden metacog_error_detection benchmark to improve discrimination (current std=0.077, target >=0.10)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_error_detection.py and data/procedural_error_chains.py
Step 2: Current error_detection has 37 chains but most models score 0.80-0.90 with tight clustering — need harder items

Step 3: Add 10 subtle error chains where the error is a plausible-but-wrong intermediate step (e.g., off-by-one in counting, sign error in physics, base-rate neglect in probability) — these should trip weaker models
Step 4: Add 5 error-free chains as foils to penalize models that over-detect errors
Step 5: Run 3-model smoke test and verify std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update the notebook repo/notebooks/metacog_error_detection.ipynb to match the updated task file

description: Re-run all 9 metacognition benchmarks against all 10 Bedrock models with hardened fok/jol/error_detection
steps: Step 1: Verify all 3 hardened benchmarks (fok, jol, error_detection) pass py_compile and import cleanly
Step 2: Run full 9-benchmark × 10-model suite using repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py with parallelism <=4 models
Step 3: Generate updated score matrix and save to repo/results/metacog_final_scores_v2.csv
Step 4: Compute per-benchmark std and verify all 9 benchmarks have std >= 0.08 (ideal >= 0.10)
Step 5: Compute overall avg std and verify >= 0.15
Step 6: Save updated discriminatory analysis to repo/sub-workflows/metacognition/results/metacog_discriminatory_summary_v2.md

description: Final writeup polish: incorporate v2 scores and regenerate cover image if scores changed significantly
steps: Step 1: Compare metacog_final_scores_v2.csv with metacog_final_scores.csv — identify benchmarks with >0.05 score shifts
Step 2: Update WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md results tables and narrative with v2 numbers
Step 3: If any benchmark scores shifted >0.10, regenerate the cover image (repo/assets/metacognition_cover.png) with updated bar chart
Step 4: Final word count check (<=1500 words)
Step 5: Proofread for consistency between score tables and narrative claims
Step 6: Commit changes to git with message describing the update
